deviations: D1 as planned plus a correctness fix the plan did not foresee (architect approved, Envoy message e25917608591a8fc36f824d4ed809f3d): Envoy's normalizer caps every review body at 2048 runes (packages/envoy/internal/contracts/normalize.go capBody/addCappedBody, the pull_request_review case) and the trailing footer of a long review is cut off, so a positive session match on the capped body would set aside every long review the reviewer itself writes. intake decodes body_truncated onto PullRequestReview.BodyTruncated; a new pre-apply hook ConsumerSpec.ReviewBody (beside ReviewPermission) restores a truncated review-App review's full body from GitHub (GET /pulls/{n}/reviews/{id}, review App token, the runtime's shared rate-limit memory honoured, unrecorded pull requests skipped) before the fact enters its transaction; a review with no id stays set aside and the set-aside log line carries body_truncated=true. Census: one GitHub read per truncated review-App review on a recorded pull request; none otherwise.

The refresh loop's lifetime is Oh My Pi's, not legion controller start's signal context: main cancels its context on SIGINT/SIGTERM and a terminal Ctrl-C reaches both processes, Oh My Pi handling it as its own and running on, so a loop bound to the signal would leave the controller on a token nobody refreshes (cmd/legion/controller_credential.go startControllerGitHubRefresh).

The contracts mirror carries LegionControllerCredentialResponse only: the plan named a request mirror too, but nothing reads it and its sibling ControllerSecretRequest has no mirror either (removed in the simplify pass).
The simplify pass skipped removing podKind.holdsGitHubCredential (now true for both kinds): the plan's design keeps the hook and its guards; the reviewer may ask for it.

Review round 1 deleted podKind.holdsGitHubCredential (previously left to the reviewer's call) and added warnOnCommit beside logOnCommit so the set-aside of a review-App review is a Warn line a log monitor can key on.
